title: 9 things I do instead of doomscrolling
start_why: 24 s of silence and quiet setup sounds (all under -40 dB, no speech) before "Why is it so hard to stop doomscrolling?"
summary: This one needs the most cleanup: she leaves long thinking gaps between lines (105 silences over 1.2 s, 6.5 minutes of silence in a 21-minute file, the longest 12.6 s). Trimming every gap to about 0.4 s takes out most of it. There are also 24 s of setup at the start, one double "scratch that" retake and one restart. After cleanup it runs about 14:46.

cuts.why: After "Just talk, even if it's awkward." she tries the next line three times: "It's better to- scratch that." / "I would take awkward talking with people over scrolling on doomscrolling. Scratch that. I'll take that again." Keeps the final take: "I'd take awkward talking with people over scrolling on social media any time, any day." (includes a 4.9 s gap).

An 8.6 s gap, then "And if you can't, if you can, it's nice to just completely quit doomscrolling." Keeps "…something completely different. ⟨0.3 s⟩ If you can, it's nice to just completely quit doomscrolling."

decisions:
- **The numbering is off and the title says 9 things.** What she says: Number one reading, two boredom, three talking with people, four friends, then "Another thing… picking up something new" (should be **five**), then "**Number eight**… long-form content" at 15:05 (should be **six**), "Number seven" physical ✓, "Number eight" meditation and prayer ✓ (journaling folded in), then reducing social media, then "And lastly… talk to the people in your life" (nine, unnumbered). Fix with on-screen numbers (1-9), or cut "Number eight," at 15:05 (it sits in continuous speech, so a number card over it is safer).
- **Pace**: trimming all 100 gaps to 0.4 s will make it feel much faster than the raw take. If it feels rushed, keep 0.6-0.8 s at the section changes (before each "Number …").
- **16:03 a stray "Yeah."** between sections (963.0-963.5): cut or keep.
- **13:21-13:34**: 17 s of near-silence with one short sound at 13:21 (801.3-802.3) that whisper didn't catch; the pause trims cover it, but listen in case it's a word.
- 11:19 "A lot of people say crocheting really helps them. But (if) I still knew how to, I would do it a lot.": fine.
kit:
**Skipped from the kit:**
- "anything you want to replace it with has to have an endpoint, or a checkpoint where you can stop, so that thing doesn't also become addictive".
- Friends: the example of "your mom will throw a party and there are so many people there" (she gives the school example only).
- Thrift store: "when I get a bag and I'm like, 'Oh yeah, see what I found.' Weirdly…" and "the interesting thing about going to a thrift store is that…".
- Picking up something new: "do not even make it something that makes money" / "we usually don't want to do things that don't make us money" (said more loosely: "habits that we cannot monetize").
- Physical: "…and it did. Yeah, I think it's something that might work".
- The numbers five and six (see decisions).

**Added:** "My screen time is already low for an average person, but I want it even lower"; she reads while she eats; Kindle/iPad aside; banana-bread baking failures; the five or seven euro bag; plants; "I'm very physically lazy"; junk journaling; "delete social media apps from my phone and use them on my desktop".

**Facts to check:** nothing factual beyond the opening claim that infinite scroll removes "natural stopping cues" (fine as stated; if she wants a source on screen, the kit's research section has it).
